extraction.design_notes: Single-center, open-label randomized clinical trial (STARDUST); outcome assessors and laboratory staff masked to group assignment; duration 6 months with follow-up at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months.

population.condition: type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease
key_inclusion_criteria: individuals 35 years or older with type 2 diabetes and a diagnosis of PAD, evaluated with Doppler ultrasonography, computed tomography angiography, or angiography in the previous 12 months
transcutaneous oxygen pressure (TcPo2) of the foot had to range from 49 to 30 mm Hg at the screening visit
optimal or suboptimal glycemic control (HbA1c ranging from 6.5% to 8%) while taking stable doses of glucose-lowering medications

evidence.quote: Fifty-five participants (mean [SD] age, 67.5 [8.5] years; 43 [78%] male and 12 [22%] female; 55 [100%] White) were randomized
individuals 35 years or older with type 2 diabetes and a diagnosis of PAD, evaluated with Doppler ultrasonography, computed tomography angiography, or angiography in the previous 12 months
30 participants were assigned to the liraglutide group
so all liraglutide group participants took 1.8 mg/d of liraglutide
27 to the liraglutide group and 28 to the control group
with significant differences favoring the liraglutide group at the end of the trial (estimated treatment difference, 11.2 mm Hg; 95% CI, 8.0-14.5 mm Hg; P < .001)

outcomes.name: proportion of patients achieving a 10% increase in TcPo2 from baseline

evidence.quote: The increase of at least 10% from baseline in TcPo2 occurred in 24 participants (89%) randomized to the liraglutide group and 13 participants (46%) assigned to the control group (relative risk, 1.91; 95% CI, 1.26-2.90; P < .001).

adverse_events.term: No participants in either group reported adverse events to any medication administered
